items.question: Which ON condition does the slide use to match student alias se to sport alias sp?
items.explanation: The slide matches the sport number in the student table to the sport number in SPORT.

context.title: Join inputs
context.content: student_enroll se (SID, SNAME, sportNO); sport sp (sportNO, sportNAME). Students are assigned sports by sport number.

items.question: How many rows does an INNER JOIN on student_enroll.sportNO = sport.sportNO return, without any additional filters?
items.explanation: The displayed inner join result contains eight rows. Students without a matching sport are not included.

items.question: What does student_enroll LEFT JOIN sport on sportNO return before any additional filtering?

options.text: All ten students, with NULL sport names for two
Eight assigned students plus three unused sports

items.explanation: The result retains all student rows, including the two whose sport name is missing.

items.question: Which join on sportNO keeps all sports, including sports with no students, but drops unassigned students when student_enroll is on the left?
items.explanation: SPORT is on the right. The right join keeps sports even when no student is enrolled.

items.question: Which rows does a FULL OUTER JOIN preserve?

options.text: Matched rows and unmatched left rows only
Matched rows and unmatched right rows only
Matched rows and unmatched rows from both sides

items.explanation: A full outer join keeps matched rows and unmatched rows from both tables.

items.question: The products table has a price column. Which filter retrieves rows priced strictly below 2.00?
items.explanation: The slide uses WHERE price < 2.00 to select products priced below 2.00. The strict inequality excludes 2.00 itself.

items.question: Which SQL operator can replace prod_price >= 50 AND prod_price <= 100?
items.explanation: BETWEEN expresses an inclusive range: values equal to the lower or upper limit are included.
